name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Quigley's incumbency and roughly $1.1M war chest against a Republican with no reported fundraising
No public general-election polling or expert ratings
model.rationale: The district's 19-point Democratic lean, Quigley's incumbency and financial edge, and a Republican campaign with no visible fundraising all point to a comfortable hold, and prediction markets price Democrats near 95 percent. Nothing in the record signals vulnerability, so the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or credible polling showing a much tighter race would be the main reason to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois's 5th District, anchored in Chicago, leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 19 points. Mike Quigley, the incumbent since 2009, is running for another term and enters the general election with roughly $1.1 million on hand after raising about $1 million. His Republican opponent, Tommy Hanson, shows no reported fundraising or cash on hand in available records, and no outside groups are active in the race.

No public polls of the general election are available, and no expert raters list the seat as competitive. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 95 percent. The combination of a strong incumbent, a heavily Democratic electorate, and a largely invisible Republican campaign points to a comfortable Quigley victory, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
